reason: The code reading is right and the one-press observation reproduces (state=owner-draft shows "Only you can see this", "Publish", "Updated 16 July 2026"; pressing Publish lands on "Mara & Finn have had this since 15 July." with the strap "The link is below."). Everything the finding builds on that is wrong or harmful. (1) The stated consequence is false. I drove the brand-new-plan path the round-8 note actually claims: state=owner-empty, type "3 October 2026", Set the day, Add a moment, Escape, Publish. It renders the draft press screen in full - headline "Send it to Aisling & Tom.", announced strap "Ready to send. The link is below.", draft card. So the draft half of the publish screen is NOT "rendered by no graded state"; it is rendered, reachable and driveable from a graded state, because setday and add set the record permanently and do not restore. The round-8 fix recorded as done is done. owner-draft is a camera position for photographing the branch, not the flow that exercises it. (2) The audit-coverage claim is inert. The draft headline and strap are the same elements, classes, ramp and weights as the published ones and are strictly shorter strings, so there is nothing audit.mjs measures - palette, weight, contrast, hit target, radius, motion, ramp, leading - that differs between the two branches. (3) The proposed fix makes the artifact worse, and the restore it deletes is load-bearing for exactly one consumer. shots.mjs and audit.mjs both page.goto per state, so a fresh document resets the fixture and neither would notice. console.shell.html does not: it switches states in place via __elevate.setState + mount with no reload. I simulated the fix in page - set F.publication to draft and F.updatedLabel to today, then switched states - and the draft record leaks into every state visited afterwards: phone, desk and print stamps flip from "Updated 15 July 2026" to "Updated 16 July 2026", and publish renders the draft branch. A seat reviewing the compiled console after touching owner-draft would then grade the wrong publish screen and the wrong audience stamps. The finding trades a seam between two deep-linked camera positions for permanent fixture drift across seven states on the surface the panel actually reviews. If anyone insists on closing the seam, the only version that does not cost that is to mutate on the press rather than at render - a capture handler on the owner-draft node that re-applies the draft record before go("publish") - which is a harness nicety, not a design change a founder can act on at 9.5.
